title: Lines, rays, segments and angles
summary: Find the rays, draw parallel and perpendicular lines on dotty paper, and compare angles with a right-angle corner.
guide: This studio is for Years 3 and 4. Children tap dots to draw lines; Undo takes back the last step.

A {{term:line-segment}} has two ends, so it can be measured. A {{term:ray}} starts at a point and goes on for ever in one direction. A {{term:line}} goes on for ever both ways. Books show "goes on" with an arrowhead, and so does the board wherever a line or ray runs off the edge.

On dotty paper a {{term:parallel}} line has the same slope: if the segment goes 3 across and 1 up, so must the parallel line. A {{term:perpendicular}} line makes a right angle with the segment; it is not always "standing up".

An {{term:angle}} is an amount of turn, not a length. Fold a sheet of paper twice to make a right-angle checker and compare angles with it: smaller is an {{term:acute-angle}}, the same is a {{term:right-angle}}, bigger is an {{term:obtuse-angle}}.

engine.letters: A B C D E F G H I J
engine.instruction-line: Tap two dots to draw a line.
engine.instruction-draw: Tap three dots: end of an arm, corner, end of the other arm.

find-rays.title: Find the rays
find-rays.prompt: Tap every {{term:ray}}. A ray has one end and goes on for ever the other way.
find-rays.hint: Look at both ends of each figure. A black dot means it stops there. An arrowhead means it goes on.
find-rays.success: Well done! The green and the red figures are rays: each has a starting point and goes on in one direction.
find-rays.why: Which of these figures could you measure with a ruler? Why not the others?
find-rays.model: Only the segments, because they have two ends. A ray never ends on one side and a line never ends on either side, so they have no length.

feedback.is-line: The blue figure has arrowheads at both ends, so it goes on both ways. That is a {{term:line}}, not a ray.
feedback.is-segment: One figure you tapped has two ends and stops at both. That is a {{term:line-segment}}. Tap it again to take it back.
feedback.missed: There is another ray. A ray can point left or right.
feedback.extra: One figure you tapped is not a ray. Tap it again to take it back.

parallel-line.title: A parallel line
parallel-line.prompt: Draw a line through the red dot that is {{term:parallel}} to segment AB.
parallel-line.hint: Count from A to B: how many across, how many up? Do the same from the red dot.
parallel-line.success: Well done! Your line is parallel to AB. However far you extend them, they never meet.
parallel-line.why: How can you be sure the two lines will never meet?
parallel-line.model: They have the same slope: 3 across and 1 up. The gap between them is the same everywhere, so they never meet.

feedback.empty: Tap the red dot first, then another dot.
feedback.not-parallel: Your line is a little steeper or flatter than AB, so if it went on it would cross it. AB goes 3 across and 1 up.
feedback.not-through: Your line is parallel, but it does not go through the red dot. Start it at the red dot.

perpendicular-line.title: A perpendicular line
perpendicular-line.prompt: Draw a line through the red dot that is {{term:perpendicular}} to segment AB.
perpendicular-line.hint: A perpendicular line makes a right angle with AB. AB goes 2 across and 1 up. Imagine turning that a quarter turn.
perpendicular-line.success: Well done! Your line is perpendicular to AB. Together they make four right angles.
perpendicular-line.why: Your perpendicular line is not standing straight up. So why is it perpendicular?
perpendicular-line.model: Perpendicular means it makes a right angle, not that it is upright. AB goes 2 across and 1 up; my line goes 1 back and 2 up. That is the same step turned through a quarter turn.

feedback.empty: Tap the red dot first, then another dot.
feedback.not-perpendicular: Your line does not make a right angle with AB. An upright line is not always perpendicular, because AB is slanted. Check with the corner of a book.
feedback.not-through: Your line does not go through the red dot. Start it at the red dot.

draw-obtuse.title: Draw an obtuse angle
draw-obtuse.prompt: Draw an {{term:obtuse-angle}}: tap the end of one arm, then the corner, then the end of the other arm. The pale square corner is there to compare.
draw-obtuse.hint: An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle: one arm sticks out past the paper corner. But it is smaller than a straight line.
draw-obtuse.success: Well done! Your angle is bigger than a right angle. It is obtuse.
draw-obtuse.why: How do you know your angle is obtuse?
draw-obtuse.model: I put the right-angle corner on the vertex. One arm lay along its edge and the other arm was outside the corner. So the angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line.

feedback.empty: Tap three dots: end of an arm, corner, end of the other arm.
feedback.is-acute: This angle is smaller than the right angle: it is an {{term:acute-angle}}. Open the second arm wider.
feedback.is-right: This is exactly a right angle. Open it a little more.
feedback.is-straight: The two arms make one straight line. An obtuse angle is a little less open than that.

biggest-angle.title: The biggest angle
biggest-angle.hint: Do not look at the arms; look at how wide the angle opens. Which one has turned the most?
biggest-angle.success: Well done! The green angle has short arms, but it is the most open.
biggest-angle.why: If we made the arms of the green angle twice as long, would the angle get bigger?
biggest-angle.model: No. An angle is how much it has turned and opened. Longer arms do not change how wide it opens.

feedback.long-arms: The orange angle has long arms, but it opens only a little. The size of an angle does not depend on the length of its arms.
feedback.right-angle: The blue angle is a {{term:right-angle}}. One of the angles is even more open than a right angle.
feedback.small-angle: The purple angle is smaller than a right angle: it is an {{term:acute-angle}}. Look for the one that opens widest.
feedback.extra: Tap only one angle: the biggest. Tap again to take one back.
